row.evidence: Grammarly's plans page compare table marks SCIM as unavailable on Free and Pro and available on Enterprise (Contact Sales); the help centre's SCIM article says "Included in: Grammarly Enterprise plans".
row.notes: Unchanged status (gated): the plans page compare table ticks SAML single sign-on, SCIM and Audit Logs API only under Enterprise (Contact Sales). Plan line-up changed since June: the page now shows Free, Pro ($12 USD, 'for eligible individuals and teams') and Enterprise; the June team plan 'Business: $15/u/mo' is no longer listed, so the team plan is now Pro. The $12 is shown without a billing period; the page's embedded plan data has an Annual '1-year Grammarly Subscription' at 144.0 USD (= $12/mo), so $12 is treated as the annual-billing monthly rate. Supported SCIM IdPs: Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, Rippling (help centre). Deprovisioning invalidates sessions, deactivates and deletes the account after 30 days. Group provisioning is on request. A License Management API (list/remove users and invitees) is Enterprise-only.

plans.name: Pro
plans.price_text: $12 USD (per member per month; billing period not shown)

auth.token_source: Grammarly admin panel > Provisioning > Configure > Activate SCIM > Create token (Rippling: request token from Support)
auth.notes: Microsoft's tutorial says 'Long lived bearer token authentication supported'; Grammarly does not state an expiry.

deprovision.data_retained: Account is deactivated (kept as an 'inactive user', re-provisionable) and removed from the subscription within about an hour, then permanently deleted after 30 days.

attributes.notes: Core list from Microsoft's Entra tutorial mapping table; CostCenter from Grammarly's SCIM article (schema URN not stated). OneLogin requires email, first and last name. Group attribute names are not documented.

roles.how: Roles are assigned via the SAML GrammarlyRole attribute; SCIM role mapping is not documented.

limitations.text: SCIM requires SAML SSO to be configured first.
SCIM group provisioning is available only on request to the CSM or Support.
Deprovisioning takes up to an hour to remove the user from the subscription.
Entra: users assigned with the Default Access role are excluded from provisioning.
Provisioning fails when the subscription has no free seats.

endpoints.purpose: Remove a user from the institution (frees the licence)

rate_limits.text: 50 requests per second per endpoint; back off on 429.

limitations.text: Admin licences cannot be removed through the API.

okta.notes: OIN page ticks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate and Group Push (read from page markup).

google.notes: Google appears in Grammarly's SSO setup list but not in the SCIM-supported IdP list.

onelogin.notes: OneLogin's connector page was not loaded; facts from Grammarly's OneLogin SCIM guide.

jumpcloud.notes: Grammarly's JumpCloud article covers SSO only; JumpCloud is not in the SCIM-supported list. JumpCloud's own page was not loaded.

conflicts.text: The SAML help article says SAML is 'Included in: Grammarly Business, Enterprise, and Grammarly for Education plans', but the current plans page (Free/Pro/Enterprise) ticks SAML only for Enterprise; Business is no longer sold on the plans page. The pricing page is used for sso_plan.
The SCIM article's intro names Okta, Azure AD and OneLogin as supported, while its 'Supported identity providers' list on the same page adds Rippling.
Grammarly's Entra guide has admins generate the SCIM token in the Provisioning page, while Microsoft's tutorial says to request the token from a Grammarly representative or support.
